bib.title: Detoxifying Language Models Risks Marginalizing Minority Voices

question: Does detoxifying language models reduce their utility disproportionately on African-American English and minority identity mentions?
hypothesis: Detoxification methods inherit spurious correlations between the toxic label and AAE or minority identity mentions from toxicity training data, so they will degrade LM quality more on that language.
contributions: Automatic (perplexity) and human evaluation showing four detoxification techniques hurt LM utility more on AAE and minority identity mentions than on WAE
Showing stronger detoxification amplifies the bias
Tracing the failure to spurious correlations in toxicity datasets, and discussing harms and possible fixes

method.summary: Four detoxification techniques (DAPT, PPLM, GeDi, output filtering) are applied to GPT-2 medium using Jigsaw Civil Comments. They are compared with the base GPT-2 by perplexity on WAE, AAE and identity-mention tweets and by MTurk pairwise preference on generated continuations of WAE and AAE prompts.
method.task: toxicity mitigation in text generation; bias evaluation

datasets.name: Jigsaw Civil Comments (Kaggle unintended bias in toxicity classification)
datasets.preprocessing: removed examples where between 10% and 50% of annotations are the toxic label (low inter-annotator agreement)

datasets.name: Groenwold et al. (2020) WAE/AAE tweet pairs
datasets.split: split into toxic and nontoxic sets by scoring WAE-AAE pairs with Perspective API

datasets.name: Minority identity mention tweets
datasets.source: Twitter API, tweets containing words from a 26-term list (Appendix A)
datasets.preprocessing: toxic tweets filtered with Perspective API, then 1,000 randomly selected

datasets.name: Human-eval prompts
datasets.source: first half of tokenized tweets from the WAE and AAE sets

other.note: smaller LM trained on nontoxic data for GeDi

models.name: DAPT / PPLM / GeDi / Filtering on GPT-2 medium

other.PPLM: toxicity classifier on LM hidden states; gradient updates hidden states at generation
other.Filtering: 10 generations, return least toxic by the PPLM classifier

training.objective: DAPT: finetune LM on nontoxic data; GeDi: finetune GPT-2 small on nontoxic data; PPLM: toxicity classifier on hidden states

other.hyperparameters: taken from the original papers for each technique (not listed)

inference.decoding: top-k sampling, k = 50, for all methods
inference.samples: Filtering: 10 generations per prompt; human eval: 1 continuation per method per prompt, each judged by 3 crowdworkers
inference.prompting: first half of a tweet as prompt

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: LM perplexity on WAE/AAE/identity-mention tweets, no generation; Filtering omitted as identical to baseline

metrics.name: AAE-WAE perplexity ratio
metrics.definition: AAE perplexity divided by WAE perplexity

metrics.name: Percent preferred over GPT-2
metrics.definition: MTurk pairwise choice of baseline vs a randomly chosen detoxified continuation on toxicity, topicality, fluency, style

eval.protocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk, 3 annotators per example; no significance test stated

availability.data: Jigsaw (Kaggle), Groenwold et al. 2020 tweets; word list in Appendix A

results.claim: All detoxification techniques generate less toxicity than baseline, but filtering performs poorly because GPT-2 rarely gives nontoxic continuations of toxic prompts.
Detoxification increases perplexity on toxic tweets a lot and on nontoxic tweets less, with the largest nontoxic increase on AAE and identity mentions.
results.note: Fig 1 numbers are unlabelled in the extracted text so no per-cell value is recorded

results.claim: Cause: toxicity datasets label AAE and identity mentions toxic at disproportionately high rates through annotation and sampling bias.
results.setup: argument, citing Sap et al. 2019 and Dixon et al. 2018

limits: Human eval uses only 50 WAE and 50 AAE prompts, with no significance testing stated
Only GPT-2 medium is studied, and only four techniques
Part of the quality drop is admitted to be domain shift (training on comments, evaluating on Twitter)
The causal claim (spurious correlations in the data) is argued, not tested by an ablation with debiased data
GeDi omega set to 0.3 for perplexity rather than the default 30
No fix is tested; authors plan to explore debiasing in future work
Claim that prompts and conditional LMs will behave similarly is conjecture
